target_customer: Businesses in Indonesia, the Philippines and wider Southeast Asia that need to accept and send payments, including large clients such as Traveloka, Wise, Wish and Grab.
problem: Low card penetration and fragmented bank rails made online payments hard in Southeast Asia; Xendit offers an API for virtual accounts, cards, eWallets, retail outlets and disbursements.
business_model: Usage based payment processing fees and disbursement fees on payment volume

founders.name: Moses Lo
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background; a search snippet from a venture firm page says he met his co-founders at UC Berkeley, but that page was not opened.

founders.name: Bo Chen
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page with no background.

founders.name: Juan Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page with no background.

competitors.name: Veritrans Indonesia (later Midtrans)
competitors.what: Online payment gateway launched in 2012 as a joint venture, later renamed Midtrans in October 2016
competitors.traction_then: Named among leading local payment gateways in May 2015 coverage; over-the-counter payments launched 2015
competitors.funding_then: Backed by VeriTrans Inc., netprice.com and a Midplaza investment arm

competitors.name: Doku
competitors.what: Payment gateway with enterprise online payments since 2007
competitors.traction_then: Partners including AliExpress and migme per May 2015 feature

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many Indonesian banks, virtual accounts and later cards and eWallets is hard operational and integration engineering, though not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Bank integrations, licenses and merchant integration create switching costs, but gateways were already competing on price.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gojek acquired Midtrans in 2017 per TechCrunch, creating a better funded rival, but Xendit still reached unicorn status in 2021.

market_need_then: Indonesia had low credit card penetration and bank transfers were the favored payment channel, so businesses needed virtual account and disbursement tools; local gateways existed but developers wanted a better API.

branding.domain_note: Uses xendit.co rather than a .com domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer and business facing, tagline Making payments simple on LinkedIn

branding.brand_signature: Positioned as a Stripe alternative built for Indonesia and Southeast Asia

rebrands.why: Payex was acquired by Xendit and rebranded under the Xendit name; this is an acquired brand, not a Xendit rebrand

branding.community_and_virality: Cited as the first Indonesian YC startup and a unicorn; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known regionally among developers and enterprise clients after the 2021 unicorn round, but no mascot or consumer brand.

pivots.from: Consumer peer to peer payment service
pivots.to: Payment gateway and API for businesses
pivots.why: Per a search result summary, the company realized the need for fund disbursement in a developing digital economy; not read in a primary source

outcome_analysis: Xendit grew from a 2015 YC start into the leading Indonesian payment infrastructure player, raising 64.6M in March 2021, 150M at a 1 billion valuation in September 2021 and 300M in May 2022, with total raised reported at 538M. It cut about 5 percent of staff in October 2022 and again later amid the downturn, but remains an independent company handling about 9 billion dollars of yearly payment volume per 2021 reporting.
notes: Series A amount of 20M in June 2018 appears only on aggregators, so the amount is null; Crunchbase News names Kleiner Perkins as lead. Series B and D details come from search snippets of Business Wire releases (not opened); Series C was read in TechCrunch which gives 238M total. Series D total 538M stated in the Business Wire release per search summary. Seed of 100K to 120K from YC in 2015 is aggregator only and unverified. TechCrunch names Tessa Wijaya as COO but does not call her a co-founder, so she is not listed. Xendit website returned 403. The Midtrans founding year conflicts across sources; 2012 from its own timeline. Layoffs reported October 2022 (5 percent) with a later round; the 2024 reorganization is noted only by a headline. Competitors sources dated May 2015, during the batch.
